items.title: Broad U.S. equity rally coexists with extraordinary Nvidia-versus-semiconductor divergence
items.summary: Barron's reported the S&P 500 up 2.3%, Nasdaq up 2.7%, and all 11 sectors positive, while Nvidia fell about 4.5% and the Philadelphia semiconductor index gained 6.6%. MarketWatch independently reported 391 S&P 500 constituents advancing. The breadth suggests a broad rebound after last week's rout, not a generalized rejection of AI infrastructure; the divergence is intraday and may narrow.

items.title: China formally extends US tariff and critical-material export-control suspensions to January
items.summary: China extended the suspension of an additional 24% tariff on US imports for two months while retaining a 10% tariff. Its commerce ministry also extended selected rare-earth, battery-material and related technology export-control waivers through January 10, 2027; port-fee suspensions were extended as well. The measures reduce immediate supply-chain policy risk but do not verify higher physical exports or permanent liberalization.

items.title: NRG rises roughly 9% as $4 billion gas generation sale and earnings gain market confirmation
items.summary: NRG advanced 9.30% to $96.50 by 11:41 AM EST after reporting adjusted EPS of $4.68 and agreeing to sell 4.9 GW of generation to LS Power for $4 billion. This is market confirmation of previously reported fundamentals, not a completed sale. Regulatory approvals, debt reduction, buybacks and 2027 earnings delivery remain key uncertainties.

items.title: Ionis drops nearly 28% as Tryngolza forecast halving hits commercialization outlook
items.summary: Ionis fell 27.83% to $28.45 at 10:35 AM EST, versus roughly 10% lower in earlier premarket reports. The company reduced Tryngolza 2026 product revenue guidance to about $50 million from $100–110 million, while reaffirming consolidated revenue guidance. The product shortfall is material; durability of prescriptions and reimbursement remain uncertain.

items.title: Iraq says U.S. understanding enables oil exports via Oman-side Hormuz lane
items.summary: Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said Baghdad reached understandings with Washington allowing crude shipments through a lane near Oman. Iraqi officials separately reported October exports near 3.5 million barrels/day versus 2.65 million in September. The diplomatic statement is a leading signal, not independently verified fresh traffic through the proposed lane; active MARAD advisories still describe high shipping threats.
